chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Umar ibn Aban, from Sa'id ibn al-Hasan, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Does one of you come to his brother, insert his hand into his purse, take what he needs, and he does not repel him?' I said: 'I do not know that among us.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Then there is nothing [to worry about].' I said: 'Then [it is] destruction?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Surely the people have not yet been given their forbearance [or wisdom/insight].'

key_terms.أَحْلَامُهُمْ: Their forbearance, wisdom, or insight (plural of hilm)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean when he says people have not yet been given their 'ahlam' in the context of borrowing?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) uses the metaphor of taking from a brother's purse to illustrate the erosion of mutual trust and social etiquette within the community of believers. He attributes the current state of affairs to the fact that the people have not yet been granted full 'ahlam' (wisdom or discernment), implying that their behavior is a result of incomplete spiritual maturity rather than inherent malice. This highlights the Shia emphasis on gradual spiritual development and the importance of preserving brotherhood through patience and proper conduct.
